assessment.nobel_worthiness: An invention in the strict sense: correcting spherical aberration of electron lenses overcame a limit recognised since Scherzer and made routine sub-angstrom imaging and atomic-resolution spectroscopy possible. Its impact on materials physics, interfaces, oxides and nanostructures is broad and lasting, and the discovery is clear and concrete.
assessment.attribution: Rose (theory of the corrector design), Haider (implementation in the TEM corrector) and Urban (first demonstrations in the Julich group) form a natural three-person configuration within the supplied credits. Other contributors such as Krivanek on the STEM side are not in the credited list, which leaves a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: commercial instruments have been in use for over two decades, results are independently confirmed in many laboratories, and recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the STEM corrector line of work (not credited here) should share recognition with the TEM corrector line.
I draw on my own field familiarity and cannot treat the credit history as independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opened new precision tests, geodesy and a route to redefining the second. The idea is original, the measurement outcome is unambiguous, and impact on metrology is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realised the lattice clock concept; Ye's group drove the strontium clock to its extreme accuracy and stability. Two laureates are a clean, defensible pairing, although ion-clock and frequency-comb contributions from others are already recognised or separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced by many national labs; recognition is timely given the redefinition of the second under discussion.
uncertainties: Whether single-ion optical clock work should be considered as part of the same discovery.
Exact timing of the redefinition of the second is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. The finding is original, clear and has driven a very large body of work.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. This theory plus experiment trio fits the supplied credits well, though other experimental groups also contributed early confirmation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by multiple groups since 2018, although the nature of the superconducting pairing remains unsettled; recognition is plausible now but still on the early side.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity is not settled.
Credit for the experimental discovery versus subsequent independent confirmations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and its realisation in HgTe wells, together with the Z2 classification, established topological insulators as a major paradigm in condensed matter physics with wide influence on materials research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theoretical foundation; Molenkamp led the first experimental observation in HgTe. This is a coherent theory plus experiment trio from the supplied names, leaving out Zahid Hasan (3D materials) and Bernevig, Zhang et al. who are not all credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature: nearly two decades of independent confirmation across materials platforms.
uncertainties: Priority disputes involving HgTe theory proposals and 3D topological insulators.
Whether Hasan or others should replace one of the proposed laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental discovery of a Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model and was a landmark, with decisive instrumental innovation in the detectors. The importance is beyond question.
assessment.attribution: The Nobel Prize was given in 2013 for the theory. Experimental recognition faces the problem of large collaborations; the founders and proposers of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are a defensible compact configuration, but spokespersons at the time of discovery (e.g. Gianotti) are an equally arguable choice.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by two experiments and later measurements; recognition is arguably late.
uncertainties: Allocation among collaboration founders, spokespersons and key analysts is contentious.
Whether the committee wishes to honour a collaboration-scale result in a three-person form.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED created strong light-matter coupling on a chip and provides the control and readout architecture of superconducting quantum processors; it is an original, important and widely used framework.
assessment.attribution: Blais (theory), Wallraff and Schoelkopf (first experimental demonstration and development) match the supplied credits. Other contributors such as Devoret and Yale colleagues may deserve consideration.
assessment.maturity: Well established, with independent experiments in many labs; the 2025 prize on macroscopic circuit quantum effects makes timing sensitive.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently recognised superconducting circuit work.
Distribution of credit within the Yale and Sherbrooke groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Independent 1987 proposals of photonic band gaps and subsequent experimental realisation of three-dimensional photonic crystals created a general approach to controlling light in structured dielectrics, with strong impact on nanophotonics.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John made the original and independent proposals; Yablonovitch also made the first microwave band gap structure. Russell and Noda are important for fibres and lasers but form different applications.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with broad independent confirmation, though the strongest impact is in applied devices rather than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the physics discovery is separable from engineering applications such as photonic crystal fibres.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in IceCube opened neutrino astronomy and provided a new messenger, including evidence for a blazar and the Galactic plane source.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project; Karle and Spiering made major contributions to detector and analysis. As with collaboration results, individual credit is difficult to separate.
assessment.maturity: Strong evidence and independent corroboration are partial: source identification is still limited, so the discovery is mature but not complete.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the roles of earlier projects such as AMANDA.
